tytul: Cornelian cherry jam (processed as NCHFP describes)
wstep: This card describes a cornelian cherry jam without added pectin from the bylena.com recipe: cornelian cherries simmered in water, pressed through a sieve and cooked with the same weight of sugar, filled into sterile jars and processed in a boiling-water bath as NCHFP describes for jam without added pectin. [T:ACI-820,ACI-625]

ostrzezenia.tekst: Store sealed jars in a cool, dark, dry place at 50–70 °F (about 10–21 °C) and, for best quality, use them within a year: NCHFP gives up to a year of best quality for jams and jellies made from a tested recipe and processed for the recommended time, and this card is not a tested recipe. [T:ACI-733]
Do not reduce the sugar: NCHFP warns that in traditional recipes too little sugar prevents gelling and may allow yeasts and molds to grow. [T:SLO-001]

sekcje.naglowek: About the fruit and the recipe
akapity: Cornelian cherries are acidic fruit: selected genotypes from Turkey had a pH of 2.87–3.12 (3-year means), and fruit from another population a pH of 2.60–4.02. [T:SUS-347]
Because fruit acidity varies, this card does not promise any particular pH for the jam; it relies on the full amount of sugar and on the NCHFP filling and processing rule. [T:SUS-347,SLO-001,ACI-625]

The bylena.com recipe is not a tested canning recipe: it pours the jam into clean, dry jars and gives no boiling-water bath or headspace; JarAtlas does not skip them and takes them from the NCHFP rule for jam without added pectin. [T:ACI-820,ACI-625]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): make the jam only from cornelian cherries, water and sugar in the proportions below, without other fruit or spices. [T:ACI-820]

According to the bylena.com recipe, the jam uses 2 kg of cornelian cherries, enough water to cover them, and sugar equal in weight to the sieved purée (about 1 kg of purée to 1 kg of sugar). [T:ACI-820]
NCHFP warns not to reduce the sugar in traditional recipes: too little sugar prevents gelling and may allow yeasts and molds to grow. [T:SLO-001]
NCHFP fills jam without added pectin into sterile jars; JarAtlas uses sterile jars at every elevation. [T:ACI-625,SLO-118]

NCHFP puts the empty jars right side up on the rack in a boiling-water canner and fills the canner and jars with hot (not boiling) water to 1 inch (about 2.5 cm) above the tops of the jars. [T:SLO-120]
To sterilize empty jars, NCHFP boils them for 10 minutes below 1000 ft, and above that 1 minute longer for each additional thousand feet. [T:SLO-118]
JarAtlas rule for metres: boil the jars for 10 minutes up to 300 m, and add 1 minute for every further 300 m or part of it. [T:SLO-119]
Cover the cornelian cherries with water, bring to the boil, then turn the heat to low and simmer for 30 minutes. [T:ACI-820]
Press the fruit through a sieve to remove the pits, and weigh the purée. [T:ACI-820]
Add the same weight of sugar, bring to the boil and simmer on low heat for 1 hour, stirring from time to time. [T:ACI-820]
Just before filling, remove and drain the hot sterilized jars one at a time. [T:SLO-120]
Fill the hot jam into the sterile jars, leaving 1/4 inch (about 0.6 cm) of headspace, seal them with self-sealing two-piece lids and process them in a boiling-water canner. [T:ACI-625,SLO-003]

Keep the water at least 1 inch (about 2.5 cm) above the jar tops during processing, and 2 inches (about 5 cm) above the jars if the processing time is over 30 minutes; if needed, add boiling water around the jars, not onto them. [T:ACI-953]
Start timing only once the water is boiling. [T:ACI-954]
If the water stops boiling at any time, turn the heat to its highest setting, bring the water back to a vigorous boil and time the whole process again from the beginning. [T:ACI-947]
Do not seal the jars with paraffin or wax: NCHFP no longer recommends paraffin or wax seals for any sweet spread, because of possible mold contamination. [T:SLO-002]
Up to 1000 ft (up to 300 m) process half-pint and pint jars for 5 minutes. [T:ACI-625,ACI-176]
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased. [T:ACI-015]
Above 1000 ft (above 300 m) process them for 10 minutes, and above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) for 15 minutes. [T:ACI-625,ACI-176]
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m. [T:ACI-176]
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage. [T:ACI-015]

When the time is up, turn off the heat, remove the canner lid and wait 5 minutes before taking the jars out; NCHFP says this wait is not needed for food safety when USDA or University of Georgia times are used. [T:ACI-955]
The NCHFP table gives times only for half-pint and pint jars. [T:ACI-625]
JarAtlas rule (cautious; the NCHFP table stops at pints): a pint holds about 473 ml, so a 0.5 l jar has no tested time in this recipe; use jars of up to 473 ml. [T:ACI-179,ACI-174]
When you take the hot jars out of the canner, do not retighten the lids or bands; this can cut through the gasket and cause seal failures. [T:SLO-210]

Cool the jars at room temperature for 12 to 24 hours, then remove only the screw bands (the metal rings of two-piece lids), leaving the flat lids on the jars, and test the seal: press the middle of the lid, and if it springs up when you release it, the jar is not sealed. [T:SLO-196,SLO-212]

NCHFP calls Mason-type canning jars with self-sealing two-piece lids (a flat lid and a screw band) the best choice, and this seal test and the method on this card assume them; NCHFP does not recommend other commercial jars whose mouths cannot be sealed with two-piece canning lids for canning any food at home. [T:SLO-223,SLO-212]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): use this card only with jars that take two-piece canning lids; it gives no method for twist-off jars or jars with glass lids, so do not use them for this recipe. [T:SLO-223]
A sealed lid is concave, curved down slightly in the centre; if the centre is flat or bulging, the jar may not be sealed. [T:SLO-196]
If a jar has not sealed at this check, keep it in the refrigerator and eat it within several days. [T:SLO-197]

Store sealed jars in a clean, cool, dark, dry place, not above 95 °F (35 °C) and not near hot pipes, a stove or a furnace, in an uninsulated attic or in direct sunlight; in such conditions the food may spoil. [T:SLO-198]
Keep opened jam in the refrigerator at 40 °F (about 4 °C) or lower. [T:SLO-018]
JarAtlas rule: keep an opened jar in the refrigerator and use it within 1 month, the time NCHFP gives for regular full-sugar cooked jams. [T:SLO-018]

Opening the jar often or leaving it out at room temperature for long periods shortens this time; you can spoon the amount you need into a bowl and put the jar back in the refrigerator quickly. [T:SLO-213]
Keep the opened jar in the refrigerator until it is used up. [T:SLO-213]
Before using a stored jar, check that the lid is tight and holds a vacuum: a good seal has a concave centre. [T:SLO-191]
Look for streaks of dried food running from the top of the jar, rising air bubbles and unnatural colour. [T:SLO-191]
When opening the jar, check for an unnatural smell, spurting liquid and cotton-like mould on the food or under the lid. [T:SLO-191]
Do not taste food from a jar with an unsealed lid or with signs of spoilage. [T:SLO-190]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): throw out such a jar. [T:SLO-190]
Discard jam with mold on it; USDA and microbiologists advise against scooping out the mold and eating the rest. [T:SLO-012]
Check an opened jar regularly for signs of spoilage such as mold, yeast or an off odor, including a fermented, yeasty or alcohol smell; if you find any, throw out the whole jar. [T:SLO-181,SLO-013]
